title: VENERABLE
author: Cooper T.
desc: Pure strength and athleticism, beginning focusing on foundations, end soaring bench press strength. Sprinting a key element as well, though it is not included in the schedule. Inspired by Gu Zhen Ren’s ‘Reverend Insanity’.

ex.note:
Most important lift. High intent, warm up thoroughly and focus on execution.

Main cues:
- “Spread the bar” close to lock-out 
- “Leg Extension” during leg-drive
- “Corkscrew the hands” during set-up
Secondary lift, push for as much weight as possible with proper execution.
Pounce hard on the descent of the crunch, then control weight on the way up to slowly regather energy, then pounce back down as hard as possible. Take 1-3 warm up sets, then push for a heavy weight.
Critical exercise. Push for as much weight as possible, don’t go too fast as you can lose your balance, brace through your chest, and keep an eye out for any imbalances.
Complete single-arm if imbalances are present. Find a good tempo.

ss.note: Focus on going as far back as *comfortably* achievable, push for a decent weight and move it explosively.
Get a good rhythm and get the volume in, although it’s uncomfortable, finish the workout strong.

ex.note: Weighted pull-ups, choose any grip you’d like (regular, wide, chin-up, neutral, etc.) and keep it for the duration of the program. Use straps as necessary.
Consider doing single leg, if so, focus on balance on explosively firing out of the bottom of portion of the lift. Stay focused and push for as much weight without form breakdown.
Machine Calf Raises, can be done on a standard machine, leg press, or even a barbell if necessary. Focus on the pump/mind muscle connection, and keep your body fresh for leg press.
Extremely heavy, maximum weight possible, treat this lift extremely seriously. Experiment with foot placements, try your normal squat stance, and be sure to push through all parts of the foot.
Push for very heavy weights, find a rhythm, be sure to use straps.
Single leg, push for solid weights and move with a good tempo. Squeeze the quads to develop mind-muscle connection. Use this time to work out imbalances in the quads.
Focus on weaknesses today; this is a general template working on mid range sticking points, with grip included. Keep fatigue low and focus on technique for this session, optimizing weak press angles.
Another weakness based lift, replace with any variation of your choosing, this is just a template if you are unsure of what to do. Record main pressing days to determine what should go here.
Start off with bodyweight and progress to more weight in the future.
Hammer this powerlifter style, cheat curls with maximum weight, use momentum and needed as push as hard as possible.
Bodybuilding style, go slow and controlled and push past the burn.
This is an activation exercise, meaning it is part of warm up. Don’t be deceived by the low RPE, still focus on moving this weight explosively, and dial in on a clean bar path.
Main lift. Push as hard as you can and try to keep a good rhythm to maximize weight over the 10 reps. Keep and eye out for imbalances.
Push heavy and keep a good tempo.
Push heavy, use a spotter to assist in some reps
Practice these bodybuilder style, slow and controlled, feeling the contraction and developing mind-muscle connection. Push to failure.
Press heavy and compromise form as needed to maximize stress on the triceps.
Push heavy and use momentum as needed, finish the workout strong.
Spend a few sets warming up to a heavy triple, this is part of the deadlift warm up so focus on recruiting the CNS and getting warm.
Consider using the Trap Bar if available. Pull the slack out, push through the quads and drive the hips through. Remember, this is a hinge, not a pull. Main lift, aim for heavy weights, 3-5 min rest.
Style is all down to personal preference; slow and controlled or explosive and heavy. Either way yield benefits, entirely up to you.
Push extremely heavy with solid form, treat this exercise very seriously and push to failure or near failure with every set. Replace with Zercher or Smith Machine squat if no access to Hack squats.

ss.note: Perform single leg and push heavy.
Focus on RFD (Rate of Force Development) at the bottom, pulling with maximum intent from the initial pull and settling into a good rhythm.
